**This skill is consumer-bound.** The runner, commands, layout, and mock seams are the
consumer repo's, never this plugin's. Two bindings, both in the consumer's `roadmap.config.json`:

1. **`testConventions`** — the repo's test runner, test file layout (colocated vs `__tests__/`),
   mock seam (which boundary to fake), fixture home, assertion style. Read it before writing any
   test. Absent → infer from 2-3 existing test files nearest the code under test and say so. (remedy: using-zeroh-roadmap/references/layout.md §Missing homes)
2. **`gateCommands`** — the `unit` / `integration` / `e2e` slots bind the commands (resolved by
   `roadmap gate run`).

Also check the consumer's own test-strategy document if one exists (e.g. `docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md`)
— it outranks the generic guidance below.

## Test Pyramid (generic shape — counts/runtimes are the consumer's)

| Tier | What | Bound by |
|------|------|----------|
| 1a — Unit | Pure logic, no I/O, colocated with source | the `unit` slot |
| 1b — Integration | Real wiring through the app's entrypoints, external boundaries faked | the `integration` slot |
| 2 — E2E | Real user journeys against a running instance | the `e2e` slot |

Push every assertion as far DOWN the pyramid as it can live: a rule provable in a unit test
does not belong in an E2E test.

## What gets a test at all — the declarative-artifact rule

The pyramid ranks WHERE an assertion lives; this rule decides WHETHER one exists. (testMode
assignment and the deviation protocol live in
`skills/using-zeroh-roadmap/references/test-worthiness.md` — the two homes must not drift.) Before writing
a test, name what a RED would mean. *A function's behavior changed* is a test. *A data file's
contents changed* is not: declarative artifacts (yaml/json/md, images, manifests, lockfiles, seed
data) get no bespoke test file, and never a byte-for-byte content assertion — that is a second
copy of the data that moves with it, guarding nothing. The honest guard for an artifact is its
INVARIANT (parses, references resolve, set exhaustive, ids unique), expressed as one more CASE in
a lane the consumer already runs (`gateCommands.ratchets` / `lint` / `emit`, or its documented
validator script). One scan extended with a case beats one new file per rule: a new `*.test.ts`
is permanently wired into the unit tier (inventory checks, coverage floors), while a lane leg is
one line.

This is NOT a carve-out for the loader, resolver, or schema parser that reads an artifact — that
is runtime logic and carries the full coverage targets below. Nor for checks that execute a
mapping function over a contract union, nor for the wired test a new governed surface owes.

## Coverage Targets

Coverage scores EXECUTABLE LOGIC only; a declarative artifact has no coverage number.

| Risk Tier | Target |
|-----------|--------|
| Core business rules / money math (as the consumer defines them) | 90%+ |
| Auth/security | 80%+ |
| New code | 80%+ minimum |

## Quality Bar

- Tests enforce INVARIANTS, not just outputs
- Tests fail if the bug existed — mentally revert the fix and check the test goes red
- No test capitulation (changing tests to match broken behavior)
- No no-op assertions (always-true checks) and no conditional assertions wrapped in `if` blocks
- Mock at the consumer's declared mock seam; verify call ARGUMENTS, not just call counts
- Boundary tests sit EXACTLY at thresholds

## E2E Rules & Patterns

consumer — look for an "E2E" section in its CLAUDE.md or test-strategy doc, and reuse its
existing spec files as the pattern source.
/** Save once, preflight before mutation, execute the reviewed bytes. Not an authorization sandbox. */
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { lstatSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, realpathSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs'
import { dirname, isAbsolute, relative, resolve, sep } from 'node:path'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
const hash = bytes => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex')
const inside = (root, path) => path === root || path.startsWith(root + sep)
const engines = {
  bash: { command: 'bash', check: ['-n'], run: ['-e', '-o', 'pipefail'] },
  python: { command: 'python3', check: ['-c', 'import ast,sys; ast.parse(sys.stdin.read())'], run: [] },
  node: { command: process.execPath, check: ['--input-type=module', '--check'], run: [] },
}
function state(cwd, path) {
  if (typeof path !== 'string' || !path || isAbsolute(path) || path.split('/').some(p => !p || p === '.' || p === '..')) throw new Error('Expected a relative file path')
  let current = cwd
  for (const part of path.split('/')) {
    current = resolve(current, part)
    try { if (lstatSync(current).isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Symlink target refused: ${path}`) }
    catch (error) { if (error.code === 'ENOENT') return null; throw error }
  }
  const stat = lstatSync(current)
  if (!stat.isFile()) throw new Error(`Expected a regular file: ${path}`)
  return { sha256: hash(readFileSync(current)), mode: stat.mode & 0o777 }
}
function check(program) {
  const engine = engines[program.kind]
  if (!engine) throw new Error('kind must be bash, python or node')
  const result = spawnSync(engine.command, engine.check, { input: program.source, encoding: 'utf8', cwd: program.cwd })
  if (result.error || result.status !== 0) throw new Error(`Preflight failed: ${result.error?.message ?? result.stderr}`)
  return engine
}
export function prepare(request, directory) {
  const cwd = realpathSync(request.cwd)
  const output = realpathSync(directory)
  if (inside(cwd, output)) throw new Error('Prepared artifacts must live outside the consumer')
  if (!Array.isArray(request.paths) || !request.paths.length || new Set(request.paths).size !== request.paths.length) throw new Error('Declare unique target file paths')
  const source = readFileSync(request.script, 'utf8')
  const program = { version: 1, cwd, kind: request.kind, source, before: Object.fromEntries(request.paths.map(path => [path, state(cwd, path)])) }
  check(program)
  const bytes = JSON.stringify(program) + '\n'
  const path = resolve(output, `${hash(bytes)}.json`)
  try { writeFileSync(path, bytes, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o400 }) }
  catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'EEXIST' || readFileSync(path, 'utf8') !== bytes) throw error }
  return path
}
export function run(path, approved = false) {
  if (!approved) throw new Error('Execution requires prior host/user approval of this artifact')
  const bytes = readFileSync(path)
  if (resolve(path) !== resolve(dirname(path), `${hash(bytes)}.json`)) throw new Error('Prepared artifact digest mismatch')
  const program = JSON.parse(bytes)
  if (program.version !== 1 || realpathSync(program.cwd) !== program.cwd || inside(program.cwd, resolve(path))) throw new Error('Invalid prepared artifact target')
  const engine = check(program)
  for (const [target, expected] of Object.entries(program.before)) {
    if (JSON.stringify(state(program.cwd, target)) !== JSON.stringify(expected)) throw new Error(`Target changed since preparation: ${target}`)
  }
  // Private execution copy of the checked bytes: children cannot consume the
  // program as stdin, and argv size limits cannot truncate large programs.
  const directory = mkdtempSync(resolve(tmpdir(), 'greenfield-program-'))
  try {
    const script = resolve(directory, program.kind === 'node' ? 'program.mjs' : 'program')
    writeFileSync(script, program.source, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o400 })
    const result = spawnSync(engine.command, [...engine.run, script], { cwd: program.cwd, stdio: ['ignore', 'inherit', 'inherit'] })
    if (result.error) throw result.error
    return result.status ?? 1
  } finally { rmSync(directory, { recursive: true, force: true }) }
}
if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  try {
    const [command, path, option] = process.argv.slice(2)
    if (command === 'prepare') process.stdout.write(prepare(JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')), option) + '\n')
    else if (command === 'run') process.exitCode = run(path, option === '--approved')

  } catch (error) { process.stderr.write(error.message + '\n'); process.exitCode = 1 }
}
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { basename, resolve } from 'node:path'

const args = process.argv.slice(2)
if (args.includes('--help')) {
  console.log('Usage: check-readme-catalog.mjs (--catalog <json> | --project-root <dir>) [--readme <file>]')
  process.exit(0)
}
const value = flag => { const i = args.indexOf(flag); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : undefined }
const readmePath = resolve(value('--readme') ?? 'README.md')
const fail = message => { console.error(message); process.exitCode = 1 }
if (!existsSync(readmePath)) fail(`nonexistent README: ${readmePath}`)
else {
  const body = readFileSync(readmePath, 'utf8')
  const block = body.match(/<!-- repo-catalog:start -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- repo-catalog:end -->/)?.[1]
  if (!block) fail('malformed README catalog')
  else {
    const tableLines = block.split(/\r?\n/).filter(line => line.trim().startsWith('|'))
    const parsedRows = [...block.matchAll(/^\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]*?)\s*\|$/gm)]
    if (parsedRows.length !== tableLines.length || parsedRows.length < 2) fail('malformed README catalog row')
    const rows = parsedRows.slice(2).map(([, name, root]) => ({ name: name.trim(), root: root.trim() }))
    const catalogPath = value('--catalog')
    const projectRoot = value('--project-root')
    let projects
    try {
      if (catalogPath) {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(catalogPath), 'utf8'))
        projects = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : parsed.projects
        if (!Array.isArray(projects)) throw new Error('shape')
        for (const project of projects) if (!project?.name || !project?.root || !existsSync(resolve(project.root))) throw new Error(`nonexistent catalog root: ${project?.root}`)
      } else if (projectRoot) {
        const root = resolve(projectRoot)
        if (!existsSync(root)) throw new Error('nonexistent project root')
        let name
        if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'))) name = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).name
        else if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'))) name = readFileSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'), 'utf8').match(/^name:\s*([^\s#]+)/m)?.[1]
        else for (const file of ['settings.gradle.kts', 'settings.gradle']) if (existsSync(resolve(root, file))) name ??= readFileSync(resolve(root, file), 'utf8').match(/rootProject\.name\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)/)?.[1]
        name ??= basename(root)
        projects = [{ name, root: projectRoot }]
      } else throw new Error('choose --catalog or --project-root')
    } catch (error) { fail(`invalid catalog shape or input: ${error.message}`); projects = null }
    const duplicate = (items, label) => {
      const seen = new Set(); for (const item of items) { if (seen.has(item.name)) fail(`duplicate ${label} name: ${item.name}`); seen.add(item.name) }
    }
    duplicate(rows, 'README')
    if (projects) {
      duplicate(projects, 'catalog')
      const byName = new Map(rows.map(row => [row.name, row]))
      const catalogNames = new Set(projects.map(project => project.name))
      for (const project of projects) if (!byName.has(project.name)) fail(`missing README project: ${project.name} (${project.root})`)
      else if (byName.get(project.name).root !== project.root) fail(`README project path mismatch: ${project.name} (${byName.get(project.name).root} != ${project.root})`)
      for (const row of rows) if (!catalogNames.has(row.name)) fail(`orphan README project: ${row.name} (${row.root})`)
    }
  }
}

# Layout — where a consumer's roadmap lives

The router (`SKILL.md`) carries the operative rule: the root is DISCOVERED, so never state a
roadmap path as a fact. This file is the mechanics, for scaffolding a consumer, writing a phase
file's import, or diagnosing a refusal.

## The root

Two candidates, in precedence order: `roadmap/` at the git toplevel (what every existing consumer
has) and `docs/roadmap/` (for a repo that keeps its workflows as sibling doc folders).

- A candidate is the root when it carries a MARKER: `roadmap.config.json` or `phases/`. An
  existing but unmarked directory is not one — a repo with a prose `docs/roadmap/` folder keeps
  reading its real `roadmap/`.
- `ROADMAP_ROOT` overrides both, absolute or relative to the repo, and is NOT probed for
  existence — an override names where the root WILL be, so `roadmap init` can scaffold into it.
- BOTH marked is a REFUSAL that names both paths and the `ROADMAP_ROOT` remedy, never a silent
  pick: two roots means two backlogs, two claim registries and two gate directories, and guessing
  one is how half a consumer's records go quietly unread.
- Neither marked resolves to `roadmap/`, so a fresh or non-consumer tree answers what it always did.

One resolver owns this — `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs` (`roadmapRoot`, `roadmapRootRel`,
`consumerSchemaPath`), with a shell twin at `hooks/lib/roadmap-root.sh` for the hooks. A scan
tripwire in `cli/lib/roadmap-root.test.mjs` keeps every other source out of the business of
spelling the root.

## Records and the schema seam

`backlog.ts`, `ROADMAP.md`, `phases/`, `arcs/`, `archive/`, `.gate/` and `arc-evals/` all sit
under the root. The schema seam resolves root-first: `<root>/lib/schema.ts`, else the legacy
`<toplevel>/lib/roadmap/schema.ts` that existing consumers vendored. Both stay supported; a
missing seam is named with BOTH paths.

A phase file at `<root>/phases/` therefore imports `../lib/schema`, an arc file at `<root>/arcs/`
the same, and `<root>/backlog.ts` imports `./lib/schema`. Relative, so a consumer needs no
tsconfig `paths` alias.

## Scaffolding

`roadmap init [--root <dir>]` — `--root` is forwarded to `scripts/scaffold-roadmap.sh` and
defaults to `roadmap`. The scaffold refuses, naming both, rather than create a second root beside
an existing one. `--root` is deliberately NOT a config key: the config lives inside the root it
would have to name.

## Missing homes

Keep each caller's documented STOP or inference behavior. If zeroh-greenfield is not installed,
use `/plugin install zeroh-greenfield@zeroh-marketplace`; then delegate home authoring and
roadmap pointer writes to `brownfield-audit`. Never create or author missing homes inline.
# Documentation rules

The one standard every doc-producing surface cites. A document that fails a rule is
edited or deleted, never explained.

## The four principles

1. **Clear and concise** — skimmable: headings, tables, bullets. No jargon, no walls
   of prose. A reader finds their answer by scanning, not reading.
2. **No duplication** — one source of truth per fact; hyperlink to it instead of
   restating it. A second copy is where staleness is born.
3. **Timeless** — concepts and patterns, never dates, version numbers, or volatile
   paths/line numbers that rot. If a fact will be false in a month, it belongs in a
   report, not a doc.
4. **Current** — an outdated doc causes more friction than a missing one. Touching a
   doc means leaving the WHOLE doc true; delete or fix stale text on sight.

## The decision bar

Docs describe the **as-built** architecture. A standalone decision record exists only
when the decision is CRITICAL — one of:

- a boundary contract (something another team or repo builds against),
- a security/privacy posture,
- expensive to reverse,

— or when the user explicitly says "document this". Every other choice lives in the
phase's `transparencyReport` and dies with the phase. An ordinary implementation
choice never mints a doc.

## Code comments are documentation too

The same bar applies in source: a comment states a non-obvious WHY in one line, or it does
not exist. Narration ("this loop now handles…"), process archaeology (phase numbers, dates,
review rounds), and restating what the code visibly does are deleted on sight — the diff
and the transparencyReport carry that story.

## Evidence is not documentation

Verification records, audit sweeps, fix logs, screenshots, parity captures: gate-report
and `transparencyReport` material. They prove work happened; they do not describe the
system. Nothing of that class lands under `docs/`.

## Examples

| Bad | Good |
| --- | --- |
| `DECISION-2026-07-14-retry-backoff.md` explaining a retry constant | the constant's own comment states the non-obvious WHY; the choice is in the transparencyReport |

  bash: { command: 'bash', check: ['-n'], run: ['-e', '-o', 'pipefail'] },
  python: { command: 'python3', check: ['-c', 'import ast,sys; ast.parse(sys.stdin.read())'], run: [] },

# Documentation rules

The one standard every doc-producing surface cites. A document that fails a rule is
edited or deleted, never explained.

## The four principles

1. **Clear and concise** — skimmable: headings, tables, bullets. No jargon, no walls
   of prose. A reader finds their answer by scanning, not reading.
2. **No duplication** — one source of truth per fact; hyperlink to it instead of
   restating it. A second copy is where staleness is born.
3. **Timeless** — concepts and patterns, never dates, version numbers, or volatile
   paths/line numbers that rot. If a fact will be false in a month, it belongs in a
   report, not a doc.
4. **Current** — an outdated doc causes more friction than a missing one. Touching a
   doc means leaving the WHOLE doc true; delete or fix stale text on sight.

## The decision bar

Docs describe the **as-built** architecture. A standalone decision record exists only
when the decision is CRITICAL — one of:

- a boundary contract (something another team or repo builds against),
- a security/privacy posture,
- expensive to reverse,

— or when the user explicitly says "document this". Every other choice lives in the
phase's `transparencyReport` and dies with the phase. An ordinary implementation
choice never mints a doc.

## Code comments are documentation too

The same bar applies in source: a comment states a non-obvious WHY in one line, or it does
not exist. Narration ("this loop now handles…"), process archaeology (phase numbers, dates,
review rounds), and restating what the code visibly does are deleted on sight — the diff
and the transparencyReport carry that story.

## Evidence is not documentation

Verification records, audit sweeps, fix logs, screenshots, parity captures: gate-report
and `transparencyReport` material. They prove work happened; they do not describe the
system. Nothing of that class lands under `docs/`.

## Examples

| Bad | Good |
| --- | --- |
| `DECISION-2026-07-14-retry-backoff.md` explaining a retry constant | the constant's own comment states the non-obvious WHY; the choice is in the transparencyReport |
| "As of v0.43.0 the console (see src/routes/console.ts:214)…" | "The console reads ledger and stores only" — the code is the line-number authority |
| A 300-line VERIFICATION.md of command outputs | the gate report carries the run; docs/ stays architecture |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scaffold-roadmap.sh — Initialize phase-driven roadmap in a project
#
# Usage: scaffold-roadmap.sh [PROJECT_DIR] [--root <dir>]
#   --root defaults to `roadmap`; `--root docs/roadmap` puts the whole consumer under
#   docs/roadmap/ beside a sibling docs folder. Everything lands UNDER the root, including the
#   schema seam — which is what lets a phase file import `../lib/schema` relatively, with no
#   tsconfig path alias. The legacy toplevel `lib/roadmap/schema.ts` seam stays recognized by
#   cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs, so existing consumers are untouched.
#
# Creates (<root> = --root, default `roadmap`):
#   <root>/lib/schema.ts     — definePhase() + Zod shapes
#   <root>/lib/registry.ts   — Phase discovery (dynamic import + validation)
#   <root>/lib/emit.ts       — Registry emission (deterministic JSON + digest)
#   <root>/ROADMAP.md        — Validation gate + git strategy
#   <root>/backlog.ts        — Ordered execution queue
#   <root>/phases/           — Empty phases directory
#   reviews/releases/         — Release review reports directory
#   scripts/pre-review.sh     — Automated pre-review checks
#   scripts/build-dashboard.sh — Review dashboard HTML generator

set -euo pipefail

PLUGIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PROJECT_DIR="."
ROOT="roadmap"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --root)
      ROOT="${2:?--root needs a directory}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --root=*)
      ROOT="${1#--root=}"
      shift
      ;;
    *)
      PROJECT_DIR="$1"
      shift
      ;;
  esac
done

# REFUSE rather than create a second root. Two marked roots is the ambiguity
# cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs refuses to resolve, so scaffolding one into existence would hand the
# consumer a repo no command can read. A marker is roadmap.config.json or phases/ — the same
# two the resolver probes.
for candidate in roadmap docs/roadmap; do
  [ "$candidate" = "$ROOT" ] && continue
  if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/roadmap.config.json" ] || [ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/phases" ]; then
    echo "scaffold-roadmap: $PROJECT_DIR already carries a roadmap root at $candidate — refusing to create a second one at $ROOT." >&2
    echo "  Two roots means two backlogs and two registries, and every command would refuse to pick between them. Scaffold into $candidate, or move it first." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "=== Scaffolding zeroh-roadmap in $PROJECT_DIR (root: $ROOT) ==="

# Create directories
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/phases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/reviews/releases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts"

# Copy <root>/lib templates — schema, registry, emit. This is the seam a phase file reaches with
# a RELATIVE `../lib/schema`; no tsconfig `paths` alias is required of the consumer.
for lib_file in schema.ts registry.ts emit.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file" ]; then
    cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/$lib_file" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
    echo "  Created $ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
  else
    echo "  Skipped $ROOT/lib/$lib_file (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Copy ROADMAP.md
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/ROADMAP.md" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/ROADMAP.md (already exists)"
fi

# Copy backlog.ts (ordered execution queue)
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/backlog.ts" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/backlog.ts"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/backlog.ts (already exists)"
fi

# Scaffold roadmap/arcs/ (OPT-IN — arcs are optional; defineArc rides along via schema.ts).
# Deliberately NOT in audit REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS: a repo without arcs is fully valid.
# The directory only, never an example arc file: anything landing here is a LIVE arc, so a
# copied example makes id A with phases [1] real in a consumer that has authored none.
# templates/example.arc.ts stays installed with the plugin as reference material.
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/arcs"

# Copy scripts
for script in pre-review.sh build-dashboard.sh generate-changelog-md.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
      cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script"
      echo "  Created scripts/$script"
    fi
  else
    echo "  Skipped scripts/$script (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Make shell scripts executable
chmod +x "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/"*.sh 2>/dev/null || true

# Wire the npm scripts the skills invoke. do-phase / plan-phase / full-code-review all run
# `<pm> emit:phases` to regenerate reviews/changelog.json; without this script the agent can't
# find it and skips the regen. Idempotent: existing scripts are left untouched.
if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/package.json" ]; then
  node - "$PROJECT_DIR/package.json" "$ROOT" <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');
const path = process.argv[2];
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
pkg.scripts = pkg.scripts || {};
const root = process.argv[3];
const want = {
  'emit:phases': `tsx ${root}/lib/emit.ts`,
  'changelog:md': 'tsx scripts/generate-changelog-md.ts',
};
let changed = false;
for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(want)) {
  if (!pkg.scripts[k]) { pkg.scripts[k] = v; changed = true; console.log('  Added package.json script: ' + k); }
  else { console.log('  Skipped package.json script ' + k + ' (already set)'); }
}
if (changed) fs.writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + '\n');
NODE
else
  echo "  No package.json found — add a script manually: \"emit:phases\": \"tsx $ROOT/lib/emit.ts\""
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Done ==="
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "  1. Ensure 'zod' + 'tsx' are in your devDependencies (the emit:phases script runs tsx)."
echo "  2. Regenerate the changelog to confirm wiring: <pm> run emit:phases"
echo "  3. Create your first phase: /plan-phase"
echo "  4. Execute it: /do-phase 1"

Create a small command-line greeter that takes a name and prints a greeting.

A beginner learning JavaScript.

Local command line with Node.js.

Keep the foundation small, runnable and understandable.

# JavaScript CLI stack

## Rationale
Plain JavaScript ES modules on Node.js match the user's learning language. The built-in test runner avoids dependency installation, compilation and bundling.

## Alternatives considered
The installed Library/CLI matrix lists tsup + node:test (compact bundling, two tools), tsdown + vitest (rich tests, extra dependency), and unbuild (convention-led multi-format output, less explicit control). These package-distribution stacks add concepts outside this beginner prototype. This proposal adapts the library-cli archetype to the user's small JavaScript-only brief, omitting its Vite TypeScript generator.

## Consequences
Run source directly; there is no compilation or type-check gate. Keep the reusable function separate from terminal I/O. Revisit bundling when distribution requires built artifacts, and TypeScript when static contracts become a product requirement.

Sources: [Node test runner](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/test.html), [Node modules](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/esm.html). This is a proposed ruling pending foundation approval.

# Contributor guide

## Conventions
Use plain JavaScript ES modules. Keep terminal I/O in `src/cli.js` and reusable greeting behavior in `src/index.js`. Follow [the test strategy](docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md). Use [the architecture index](docs/architecture.md) for rationale. Future development uses the Roadmap phase system after foundation initialization.

## Don’t
Do not add frameworks, dependencies, UI, cloud or CI/release workflows without a new requirement. Never replace an existing home silently.

## Generalize-forward
Extract a module when a new responsibility exists. Keep the beginner's runnable path simple. Flag-first delivery applies if delivery is later selected; keep release-only work in `hold[]` until then.

## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/home/patrik/.codex/skills/.system`
- `r1` = `/home/patrik/.codex/plugins/cache/mojko-plugin-eval`
- `r2` = `/home/patrik/.codex/plugins/cache/mojko-plugin-eval/zeroh-greenfield/1.0.0/skills`
- `r3` = `/home/patrik/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote`
- `r4` = `/home/patrik/.codex/plugins/cache/zeroh-marketplace/zeroh-roadmap/0.39.1/skills`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
- deep-research-work:deep-research: Conduct thorough research using authoritative sources and produce evidence-backed findings with citations. Use this skill only when the user asks specifically for Deep research, uses $deep-research, or selects Deep research in Work mode. Do not use it for ordinary research requests. (file: r3/deep-research-work/0.1.14/skills/deep-research/SKILL.md)
- plugin-management:plugin-management: Discover and suggest relevant plugins, inspect app permissions and dependencies, and manage plugin connections or removal. Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access. (file: r3/plugin-management/0.1.0/skills/plugin-management/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-design:blade-design: Blade Labs branded UI and collateral generator. Use when building any frontend UI — pages, components, dashboards, apps, landing pages — or creating marketing collateral such as social cards, announcement banners, or branded assets. (file: r1/zeroh-design/local/skills/blade-design/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-greenfield:brownfield-audit: Handle requests phrased as audit, fill gaps, or reconcile an established repository by proposing only missing, partial, or stale homes before approval. (file: r2/brownfield-audit/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-greenfield:greenfield-init: Handle requests phrased as initialize, scaffold, or create a new repository through an approval-gated setup with sourced stack, design, standards, and roadmap pointers. (file: r2/greenfield-init/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision: Handle requests phrased as choose stack, mobile stack, or compare frameworks by presenting sourced alternatives without defaults and returning an ADR ruling. (file: r2/stack-decision/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-greenfield:using-zeroh-greenfield: Route requests phrased as init, scaffold, brownfield audit, fill gaps, or stack choice to the owning zeroh-greenfield skill. (file: r2/using-zeroh-greenfield/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Arc Sweep: Pre-merge sweep for a built arc: dispose every accumulated compromise (reusing release-sweep's debt vocabulary) and run one whole-arc software-architect review against the arc's singleSeams + designRefs, then report merge-readiness. (file: r4/arc-sweep/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Audit Roadmap: Read-only structural audit across roadmap state and the vendored schema (17 checks). Reports findings only — never fixes. (file: r4/audit-roadmap/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Do Arc: Execute a whole arc end to end: launch one per-plane workflow at a time, own the halts it hands back, sweep + validate in-session, and land via the CLI. (file: r4/do-arc/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Do Phase: Execute a roadmap phase task-by-task with enforced sequential discipline: one task = one commit + a transparencyReport, then the kind-selected gate. (file: r4/do-phase/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Eval Arc: Score a landed arc across the seven ratified dimensions — code confidence, verified-vs-intent, standards adherence, doc brevity, composability/testability, speed, plan quality — into a typed, dated ArcEvalReport ratcheted against a rolling baseline. The standalone door onto do-arc's Step 9, for arcs that landed without it. (file: r4/eval-arc/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Plan Arc: Plan a whole arc (a named, contiguous block of phases shipped as one unit): author the Arc entity, resolve the design-first gate WITH the user (reuse / new design / inherited ratified prototype / recorded skip), plan every member phase against that design, review each independently, queue one arc tier. Triggers: 'plan arc', '/plan-arc', 'create arc', 'new arc'. Not this skill: one standalone phase (plan-phase) or executing an existing arc (do-arc). (file: r4/plan-arc/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Plan Phase: Create a new roadmap phase. Use when user says: create phase, plan phase, add to roadmap, new phase, add feature, create task. Reads the code first, pre-makes every decision, rehearses verifies in both directions, then writes and commits a .phase.ts file. Not this skill: planning a multi-phase arc (plan-arc, which loops plan-phase per member) or queueing/auditing an existing phase (review-phase owns the queue). (file: r4/plan-phase/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Release Sweep: Review and resolve outstanding debts for a release version, then optionally archive the version's done phases. Run before every minor/major; optional before patches. Patch releases are never blocked on debts; archive is. (file: r4/release-sweep/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Review Phase: Independently verify a roadmap phase or whole arc against the real code: backlog phases get a plan-quality review that repairs the plan and queues it; done/in-progress phases get a report-only post-execution audit. Trigger: 'review phase N', '/review-phase N', 'verify/audit phase N', 'review arc <ID>'; also the mandatory pre-queue pass after plan-phase and the spawned judge step in plan-arc. Not for general diff/PR review or bug hunting - that is a plain diff review (the code-reviewer agent). (file: r4/review-phase/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Test Strategy: Test pyramid, coverage targets, and conventions. Use when writing tests, reviewing test quality, or planning test phases. (file: r4/test-strategy/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Using zeroh-roadmap: ALWAYS ACTIVE. Phase-driven development plugin. MUST be used when user says: create phase, plan phase, do phase, roadmap, review phase, code review, what's next, arc, sweep, backlog. Routes ALL development task requests through the phase system. (file: r4/using-zeroh-roadmap/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:Validate Arc: Drive a built arc's real shipped flow and judge it against its acceptance criteria with an independent judge panel, reporting PASS/GAPS. The terminal intent gate do-arc runs after arc-sweep, before merge. (file: r4/validate-arc/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:full-code-review: Whole-codebase pre-release audit. Parallel agents cover security, dead code, duplication, performance, architecture, edge cases, data flow, and domain-critical calculations; findings become a release verdict (any critical blocks), a remediation phase, and a review-record round. Use for "full code review", "pre-release audit", a pre-prod checkup on worry areas, or before merge-to-main/prod deploy. Not this skill: diff/phase review (code-review); a consumer's own release-review supersedes this. (file: r4/full-code-review/SKILL.md)
- zeroh-roadmap:handoff: Routes unfinished session context into durable roadmap artifacts, leaving only justified residue for a fresh session. Use for requests to hand off work, hand off to a fresh session, continue in a new session, write a context file, or produce a one-line prompt. (file: r4/handoff/SKILL.md)

---
name: brownfield-audit
description: Handle requests phrased as audit, fill gaps, or reconcile an established repository by proposing only missing, partial, or stale homes before approval.
---

# Brownfield audit

Use this workflow for an established repository. Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting, then resolve `skills/greenfield-init/references/standards.md` and `skills/greenfield-init/references/pointers.md` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root as the contract owners. Read `references/marker-table.md`, `references/harness-files.md`, and `references/readme-reconcile.md` when their stages say so.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, marker-free repositories through `greenfield-init`, and unresolved stack selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-33.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 fixture and oracle evidence.

## Detect

Confirm the repository root and inspect every evidence glob in `references/marker-table.md`. A marker is evidence, not a stack decision; absence never proves a stack. Inventory existing canonical homes and sibling-plugin availability. Resolve roadmap roots using the marker-table procedure; require the same read-only capability preflight as greenfield-init before proposing config changes. Do not call stack-decision to replace a proven existing choice.

Apply these failure exits:

- zeroh-roadmap absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace`.
- Only when an approved Blade handoff requires it: zeroh-design absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace`. Continue non-Blade documentation and configuration repairs without this sibling.
- greenfield-init absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-greenfield@zeroh-marketplace`.
- Repository root unresolved: STOP and name the unresolved path.

## Gap table

Inspect architecture, stack, test strategy and a runnable development path first. Missing documentation is an offer to improve the project, not a reason to replace working code. Expand detection categories into one row per applicable artifact (PRD, tech-stack ADR, design-system ADR, CODE-STYLE, architecture index, UX canon, README catalog, each harness file, and roadmap config), plus each independently actionable stale/partial asset. Alternative canonical homes count as present; inspect their contents before classifying. Optional framework or Superpowers absence is not a gap unless selected by the approved project requirements. Emit rows with columns `Artefact | State | Evidence path | Proposed action | Existing home to LINK`. Classify each row `present`, `partial`, `missing`, or `stale`; cite concrete evidence. Consult `references/harness-files.md` for harness rows and `references/readme-reconcile.md` for catalog currency.

## Propose

Emit proposals ONLY for gap-table rows in state `missing`, `partial`, or `stale`.
Emit no proposal for a `present` row.
Record approval before any write.

For each eligible row, show the target, source facts, minimal delta, preservation guard, and verification. Do not select a new stack or duplicate an owner contract.

## Approval

The user may accept all, choose individual rows, or decline all improvements. Reuse existing explicit scope approval. For a subset, execute independent accepted rows; explain a dependency before requesting any additional scope. Do not turn a declined suggestion into a mandatory gate or create a new arc. If approval is absent or ambiguous, return the proposal without writes.

## Act

Apply only approved gap rows. An existing home is LINKED from the index/canon, never replaced. Follow `skills/greenfield-init/references/standards.md` for conventions and generated blocks, and `skills/greenfield-init/references/pointers.md` for roadmap configuration. Call `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` if stack evidence conflicts; never infer a replacement stack.

For harness reconciliation, execute the approved pointer diffs in `references/harness-files.md`. For README reconciliation, use only the checker named in `references/readme-reconcile.md`.

## Verify

Run every approved row's falsifiable check. Re-run the README checker when applicable, byte-compare generated harness marker blocks, and confirm present rows remain unchanged. On any red result, STOP and report the row, command, and evidence without marking it complete.

## Done

Return the final five-column gap table, approval record, changed paths, verification commands and exit codes, linked canonical homes, and any stopped rows. Done exists only when this artifact is complete and every acted row is green.

Emit its parser-bound form with concrete values:

```json
{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"writes":["<repository-relative-path>"],"gaps":["<artifact>: <missing|partial|stale>: <evidence-path>"]}
```

Record declined/deferred suggestions separately from acted rows; completion of accepted rows does not claim all gaps were fixed. On an idempotent rerun with no remaining applicable gaps emit empty `proposals`, `writes`, and `gaps`. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` enforces native event ordering and observed writes; treat gap-only preservation as honor-system. Treat sibling routing, approval interpretation, and every other unbound STOP/ONLY/never rule as honor-system.

export function greet(name) {
  return `Hello, ${name}!`;
}
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greet } from './index.js';

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
if (args.length === 1 && args[0] === '--help') {
  console.log('Usage: node src/cli.js <name>');
} else if (args.length !== 1 || !args[0].trim()) {
  console.error('Usage: node src/cli.js <name>');
  process.exitCode = 1;
} else {
  console.log(greet(args[0].trim()));
}
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { greet } from '../src/index.js';

test('greets the supplied person, preserving spaces and Unicode', () => {
  assert.equal(greet('Ada'), 'Hello, Ada!');
  assert.equal(greet('Grace Hopper'), 'Hello, Grace Hopper!');
  assert.equal(greet('José'), 'Hello, José!');
});
{
  "name": "learning-greeter",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "engines": { "node": ">=22" },
  "scripts": { "start": "node src/cli.js", "test": "node --test" }
}
# Architecture

`src/cli.js` reads arguments, validates one nonblank name, trims surrounding whitespace and prints the result of `greet` from `src/index.js`. The greeting function has no I/O. This split keeps JavaScript string interpolation easy to learn and test.

Canonical records: [stack rationale](adr/0001-tech-stack.md), [design decision](adr/0002-design-system.md), [test strategy](TEST-STRATEGY.md). Extend by keeping terminal I/O in the adapter and reusable behavior in the function; add another module only when a distinct responsibility emerges.
# Test strategy

Use Node's built-in test runner and strict assertions, with tests in `test/*.test.js`. Run `node --test`. The single test checks supplied-name substitution, spaces and Unicode. A red test means greeting behavior has changed; a hard-coded greeting fails the distinct-name cases. No mocks or fixture files are needed.

The pure function is the unit boundary. Run `node src/cli.js --help` separately for CLI wiring, and `node src/cli.js Ada` for the documented success signal. These smoke commands do not claim full CLI branch coverage.

Lint, static types, compilation, browser E2E and phase emission are absent because the local JavaScript prototype needs none of those toolchains. Validate the README catalog with its supplied checker. Configuration validation belongs to the Roadmap CLI after its generated config is inspected and bound.
# Learning greeter

A small JavaScript command-line exercise. Requires Node.js 22 or newer; no dependency installation is needed.

From this directory:

```sh
node src/cli.js Ada
node src/cli.js "Grace Hopper"
node src/cli.js --help
node --test
node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --project-root .
```

The first command prints `Hello, Ada!`. Quote names containing spaces. Missing, blank or multiple arguments print usage to stderr and exit with status 1.

# Product requirements

## Product
Create a small command-line greeter that takes a name and prints a greeting.

## Audience
A beginner learning JavaScript.

## Platforms
Local command line with Node.js.

## Constraints
Keep the foundation small, runnable and understandable.

## Non-goals
UI, cloud hosting, CI and release workflows.

## Success signals
The documented command in [README](../README.md) runs the prototype; one meaningful automated test passes.

## Brand
No UI or Blade branding.

## Decisions
The product packet supplies the scope. Stack rationale is in [the stack record](adr/0001-tech-stack.md).

### Foundation approval
The fixture owner responded:

> APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN
>
> Fixture-owner ruling: approve the plain-JavaScript adaptation and exactly the listed foundation scope.

Approved scope: package.json, src/index.js, src/cli.js, test/greet.test.js, README.md, docs/PRD.md, docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md, docs/adr/0002-design-system.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/ux-canon.md, docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs and roadmap/roadmap.config.json.

The ruling authorizes config-only initialization, the reviewed foundation writer, the checker copy and prototype/test/help/catalog checks. The dependent config merge and this approval-record update require separate review before execution. Config validation follows application of the reviewed bindings. This record does not grant that dependent execution approval.

CI/release setup and cloud delivery remain deferred. No plugin-source edits, commits, deployments, subagents or other external product writes are authorized.
# JavaScript CLI stack

## Rationale
Plain JavaScript ES modules on Node.js match the user's learning language. The built-in test runner avoids dependency installation, compilation and bundling.

## Alternatives considered
The installed Library/CLI matrix lists tsup + node:test (compact bundling, two tools), tsdown + vitest (rich tests, extra dependency), and unbuild (convention-led multi-format output, less explicit control). These package-distribution stacks add concepts outside this beginner prototype. This proposal adapts the library-cli archetype to the user's small JavaScript-only brief, omitting its Vite TypeScript generator.

## Consequences
Run source directly; there is no compilation or type-check gate. Keep the reusable function separate from terminal I/O. Revisit bundling when distribution requires built artifacts, and TypeScript when static contracts become a product requirement.

Sources: [Node test runner](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/test.html), [Node modules](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/esm.html). The fixture owner approved this plain-JavaScript adaptation with the foundation scope; see [the approval record](../PRD.md#foundation-approval).
# Design system

No visual design system applies: the user explicitly selected CLI-only with no UI or Blade branding. Terminal behavior lives in [the UX canon](../ux-canon.md). Revisit if a graphical interface becomes part of the product.
# Terminal interaction

The [README commands](../README.md#commands) define usage. A successful greeting is one stdout line. Invalid input sends usage to stderr with exit status 1. `--help` prints usage and succeeds. Copy uses plain language. Visual fonts, palette, spacing, tokens and a visual quality exemplar do not apply.
# Contributor guide

## Conventions
Use plain JavaScript ES modules. Keep terminal I/O in `src/cli.js` and reusable greeting behavior in `src/index.js`. Follow [the test strategy](docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md). Use [the architecture index](docs/architecture.md) for rationale. Future development uses the Roadmap phase system after foundation initialization.

## Don’t
Do not add frameworks, dependencies, UI, cloud or CI/release workflows without a new requirement. Never replace an existing home silently.

## Generalize-forward
Extract a module when a new responsibility exists. Keep the beginner's runnable path simple. Flag-first delivery applies if delivery is later selected; keep release-only work in `hold[]` until then.

# Product requirements

## Product
Create a small command-line greeter that takes a name and prints a greeting.

## Audience
A beginner learning JavaScript.

## Platforms
Local command line with Node.js.

## Constraints
Keep the foundation small, runnable and understandable.

## Non-goals
UI, cloud hosting, CI and release workflows.

## Success signals
The documented command in [README](../README.md) runs the prototype; one meaningful automated test passes.

## Brand
No UI or Blade branding.

## Decisions
The product packet supplies the scope. Stack rationale is in [the stack record](adr/0001-tech-stack.md).

### Foundation approval
The fixture owner responded:

> APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN
>
> Fixture-owner ruling: approve the plain-JavaScript adaptation and exactly the listed foundation scope.

Approved scope: package.json, src/index.js, src/cli.js, test/greet.test.js, README.md, docs/PRD.md, docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md, docs/adr/0002-design-system.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/ux-canon.md, docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs and roadmap/roadmap.config.json.

The ruling authorizes config-only initialization, the reviewed foundation writer, the checker copy and prototype/test/help/catalog checks. The dependent config merge and this approval-record update require separate review before execution. Config validation follows application of the reviewed bindings. This record does not grant that dependent execution approval.

CI/release setup and cloud delivery remain deferred. No plugin-source edits, commits, deployments, subagents or other external product writes are authorized.
# JavaScript CLI stack

## Rationale
Plain JavaScript ES modules on Node.js match the user's learning language. The built-in test runner avoids dependency installation, compilation and bundling.

## Alternatives considered
The installed Library/CLI matrix lists tsup + node:test (compact bundling, two tools), tsdown + vitest (rich tests, extra dependency), and unbuild (convention-led multi-format output, less explicit control). These package-distribution stacks add concepts outside this beginner prototype. This proposal adapts the library-cli archetype to the user's small JavaScript-only brief, omitting its Vite TypeScript generator.

## Consequences
Run source directly; there is no compilation or type-check gate. Keep the reusable function separate from terminal I/O. Revisit bundling when distribution requires built artifacts, and TypeScript when static contracts become a product requirement.

Sources: [Node test runner](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/test.html), [Node modules](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/esm.html). The fixture owner approved this plain-JavaScript adaptation with the foundation scope; see [the approval record](../PRD.md#foundation-approval).
# Design system

No visual design system applies: the user explicitly selected CLI-only with no UI or Blade branding. Terminal behavior lives in [the UX canon](../ux-canon.md). Revisit if a graphical interface becomes part of the product.
# Terminal interaction

The [README commands](../README.md#commands) define usage. A successful greeting is one stdout line. Invalid input sends usage to stderr with exit status 1. `--help` prints usage and succeeds. Copy uses plain language. Visual fonts, palette, spacing, tokens and a visual quality exemplar do not apply.
# Contributor guide

## Conventions
Use plain JavaScript ES modules. Keep terminal I/O in `src/cli.js` and reusable greeting behavior in `src/index.js`. Follow [the test strategy](docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md). Use [the architecture index](docs/architecture.md) for rationale. Future development uses the Roadmap phase system after foundation initialization.

## Don’t
Do not add frameworks, dependencies, UI, cloud or CI/release workflows without a new requirement. Never replace an existing home silently.

## Generalize-forward
Extract a module when a new responsibility exists. Keep the beginner's runnable path simple. Flag-first delivery applies if delivery is later selected; keep release-only work in `hold[]` until then.

# Product requirements

## Product
Create a small command-line greeter that takes a name and prints a greeting.

## Audience
A beginner learning JavaScript.

## Platforms
Local command line with Node.js.

## Constraints

UI, cloud hosting, CI and release workflows.

The documented command in [README](../README.md) runs the prototype; one meaningful automated test passes.

# JavaScript CLI stack

## Rationale
Plain JavaScript ES modules on Node.js match the user's learning language. The built-in test runner avoids dependency installation, compilation and bundling.

## Alternatives considered
The installed Library/CLI matrix lists tsup + node:test (compact bundling, two tools), tsdown + vitest (rich tests, extra dependency), and unbuild (convention-led multi-format output, less explicit control). These package-distribution stacks add concepts outside this beginner prototype. This proposal adapts the library-cli archetype to the user's small JavaScript-only brief, omitting its Vite TypeScript generator.

## Consequences
Run source directly; there is no compilation or type-check gate. Keep the reusable function separate from terminal I/O. Revisit bundling when distribution requires built artifacts, and TypeScript when static contracts become a product requirement.

Sources: [Node test runner](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/test.html), [Node modules](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/esm.html). The fixture owner approved this plain-JavaScript adaptation with the foundation scope; see [the approval record](../PRD.md#foundation-approval).
# Design system

No visual design system applies: the user explicitly selected CLI-only with no UI or Blade branding. Terminal behavior lives in [the UX canon](../ux-canon.md). Revisit if a graphical interface becomes part of the product.
# Terminal interaction

The [README commands](../README.md#commands) define usage. A successful greeting is one stdout line. Invalid input sends usage to stderr with exit status 1. `--help` prints usage and succeeds. Copy uses plain language. Visual fonts, palette, spacing, tokens and a visual quality exemplar do not apply.
# Contributor guide

## Conventions
Use plain JavaScript ES modules. Keep terminal I/O in `src/cli.js` and reusable greeting behavior in `src/index.js`. Follow [the test strategy](docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md). Use [the architecture index](docs/architecture.md) for rationale. Future development uses the Roadmap phase system after foundation initialization.

## Don’t
Do not add frameworks, dependencies, UI, cloud or CI/release workflows without a new requirement. Never replace an existing home silently.

## Generalize-forward
Extract a module when a new responsibility exists. Keep the beginner's runnable path simple. Flag-first delivery applies if delivery is later selected; keep release-only work in `hold[]` until then.
